hypothesis: A VCP breakout that quickly loses its pivot but later rebuilds a quiet, narrow range around the same pivot contains renewed demand evidence. Waiting for that causal retrigger may reduce immediate stop-outs while preserving the right-tail payoff mechanism.
unique_change: Use the frozen vcp_leader_breakout candidate stream, pivot, market regime, ranking, exits, costs and portfolio rules; replace the initial-breakout entry with the original Quants failed-breakout recovery state machine.
causal_contract: A setup becomes observable only on its frozen breakout close. Failure and each recovery condition use completed bars at or before the signal timestamp. A qualifying close is filled at the next tradable open.

source_method.failure: low below 97.5% of pivot or close below 99.2% of pivot
source_method.recovery_wait_bars: 3 through 30 asset trading bars after failure
source_method.retrigger: latest close within 98.5%-102% of pivot; recent post-failure range <=7%; recent low >=97.2% of pivot; at least two near-pivot closes; recent mean volume <=108% of current 20-bar mean

stop_condition: Run this frozen method once. If the sample or failure-path gate is not met, stop this entry direction; do not vary its windows or thresholds on the exposed interval.
development_note: The entire interval is exposed development data. This is a method diagnosis, not independent validation or live qualification.
